question: Does randomly withholding learned RL increments reduce functional layer dependence and improve held-out performance?
scope: Four-action arithmetic contextual-bandit RL, not open-ended reasoning or a reproduction of the 1.5B-8B paper.
parameterization: Frozen pretrained weights; identical rank-8 LoRA on q/k/v/o and gate/up/down projections in 24 layers; alpha=16; embedding and head frozen.

arms.all: Update all 24 layer adapters; deterministic full adapter forward.
arms.middle: Update only layers 9-14; deterministic full adapter forward.
arms.rotate: Each step update 18 of 24 randomly selected layers; every learned increment remains in the forward pass.
arms.delta_drop: Each step omit learned increments in 6 of 24 layers; update the remaining 18; pretrained weights unchanged; no inverted-dropout scaling. Deploy with all increments present.

training.objective: One-update on-policy group-relative policy gradient; 8 actions per question, binary correctness, group population-standard-deviation normalization, exact 4-action KL penalty to pretrained policy with beta=0.1.
training.tuning: Seed 0, 200 steps for each arm at learning rates 3e-5 and 1e-4; choose by validation expected reward only; final main checkpoint fixed in advance.

data.version: v3: blocks of 4 distinct questions with identical ordered options, exactly one correct answer per letter
data.deduplication: No shared arithmetic identity across splits, including commutative swaps; each 4-question block has all 4 labels, the same ordered choices and the same operation. Any question-blind options-only rule achieves exactly 25% on complete blocks.
data.ood: Equal average of held-out word-format and larger-operand test scores.

mechanism_measure: On 32 complete ID test choice blocks (128 questions), remove each whole-layer learned increment separately. Record expected-reward drop and KL from full policy. Positive-drop concentration is a non-additive sensitivity proxy, not a causal partition of RL gains.
shortcut_control: Cycle held-out questions within each operation while retaining original options and reward labels. A large accuracy collapse supports actual use of question content; check balanced min/max-option heuristics and report this control.

decision_rules.informative_learning: All-layer RL should improve ID greedy accuracy by at least 3 percentage points over its pretrained baseline; otherwise classify as weak or failed learning signal.
decision_rules.concentration_prerequisite: Inspect whether baseline all-layer adapters have concentrated functional sensitivity; report whether it is centered in middle layers instead of assuming it.
decision_rules.promising_performance: Delta-drop OOD greedy accuracy at least 2 percentage points above all-layer RL on average, positive direction in all 3 paired seeds, and ID loss no worse than 2 points. Also compare to fixed-middle and rotate controls.
decision_rules.mechanism_support: Performance gain alone does not validate dispersion. Require reduced worst single-layer expected-reward loss and more effective positive-contribution layers; report paired uncertainty.
decision_rules.limits: Three seeds and synthetic one-token actions establish only pilot evidence. No novelty claim or long-reasoning generalization claim.
